Verse 17

The descent of water and the flowing of streams with it is a meaning of the same kind and nature as lightning, thunder and clouds. In the preceding scene, mention was made of thunder and lightning and of heavy clouds. Both are part of the common natural phenomena of this universe, and most of the theme of this surah revolves around them. Through these scenes is also manifested the power, dominance and grip of Allah, the One, the Subduer (al-Qahhar). The streams flow each according to its measure, each according to its capacity.

This shows that Allah has set a measure for everything. Every stream and river also has a fixed quantity of water. This is the wise governance of Allah, which is the special theme of this surah. The circle, theme and scene of this parable are those that are commonplace and that people see day and night; this scene passes before their eyes, yet like the blind they do not reflect upon it, nor do these scenes stir their hearts.

Before our eyes the water keeps falling, the rivers and streams keep flowing, and they keep carrying away the refuse of this world with them. Foam also keeps rising on these streams, so much so that at times the water is hidden and mountains of foam stand up. But this foam has no reality, it has no weight. The water that remains beneath the foam keeps flowing at its own pace, with great tranquility and in an orderly way. Then this water has a benefit within it: goodness, life and freshness. The same is the case with the metals and treasures that are melted. From them manufactured goods are made, tools are made, and they become beneficial for human life, such as iron, copper and lead, and so on. Foam also rises on these, which is worthless and is thrown away, while the pure substance remains below. When the foam subsides, the real thing emerges from beneath.

This is the parable of truth and falsehood in the life of this world. The manifestation and scene of falsehood often appears; it rises, it swells, it runs and hurries about, and it appears to have great flow. But this falsehood is like foam, or like a filthy and foul matter, and is thrown away like refuse, or it vanishes; it has neither solid reality nor any stability or firmness within it. Whereas truth is always dignified, steady and firm. At times there is a doubt that it has settled, that it has become rigid, or even that it has ended. Its stillness is a sign of death. But truth always remains in the world, just as water remains, and foam vanishes; and just as melted material remains in its original state and benefits people, while its foam or refuse vanishes, so truth endures.

﴿Thus does Allah set forth parables﴾ (13:17). Thus Allah determines the outcome of every call and every movement; the outcome of every ideology and of the struggle to revive it is of this kind. Allah deals with the deeds and words of people in this same way. He is the Governor of the universe, the One Sovereign and the Subduer. He also governs the conflict between truth and falsehood, and He has established this law of nature: that in the end falsehood must perish and truth must prevail.

Therefore, keep this firmly in mind: those who responded to the truth will have a good end. And those who rejected the call to truth are going to face a most dreadful and terrifying end. Their condition will be such that if any of them were to own the whole earth and the heavens, he would be fully ready to ransom himself from the punishment of that Day; but where would he have the earth and the heavens to give? Their reckoning will be humiliating, their abode will be Hell, and what an evil abode it will be.

Verse 18

Here, the people who accept the call of truth are set in contrast with those who refuse it. For those who refuse, there is a reckoning of evil (su' al-hisab) in place of the good (husna), and in place of Paradise there is the wretched resting place (bi'sa al-mihad). This method of speaking by contrast is observed throughout this surah.

Lesson No. 113: At a Glance

The first part of this surah dealt with the horizons of this universe, the depths of the unseen world, the wonders of the human self, and reflection upon them. In this second part, the subjects are the perceptions of human intuition, the conclusions reached by human reason, and very subtle and profound reflection, especially on the truths concerning messengership (risalah), the office of the Messenger, and divine revelation (wahy), the doctrine of Tawhid and the refutation of shirk, the ignorance of people and their demands for miracles, and haste regarding the occurrence of the Resurrection. The themes are the same as in the first part; however, the journey is through a different valley, namely the valley of intellect and understanding.

In this part, the journey begins in the valley of disbelief and faith. In the valley of disbelief there is darkness like a moonless night, while in the valley of faith there is light like the brightness of broad daylight. The one contains knowledge, and the other contains darkness and ignorance. After this, the discourse turns to the characteristics and signs of the disbelievers and the qualities and disposition of the believers, and then a scene from the witnessing of the Resurrection appears, in which the rewards of the people of Paradise and the punishment of the people of Hell are mentioned. In between, the subject of abundance of provision and restriction of provision is also discussed, and both conditions befall people in accordance with the will of Allah. A gathering is held with those whose hearts are at peace with the remembrance of Allah. Then comes the mention of the attributes of the Noble Qur'an and its power: it is near that mountains would move under its influence, it is near that the earth would split apart out of fear, and it is near that the dead would also speak. Then there is the punishment and calamities that befall the disbelievers, or that descend upon other nations near their lands, yet these people do not take warning. Then there is a humorous style of speech about their gods, then a brief tour through the valleys of the nations that were destroyed, whose places and sites of destruction are close to them. At the end, they are warned of the outcome that awaits them with impatience, because they are denying the true Messenger. Well then, let us go on to that known outcome, if they do not believe.

From this it becomes evident that the blows that were struck in the first part to shake the intellect and understanding have, in this second part, produced a considerable effect, and now the intellect has begun to think. The doors of human reason have opened somewhat, and man has begun to think about the call of Islam. Therefore, the two parts of this surah are connected with each other. That is, both parts of this surah are plucking the strings of human intellect and understanding so that human perception and reason may function.

The first issue in this part is the issue of divine revelation (wahy). It was touched upon at the beginning of this surah as well. Here it is reconsidered, in a very fresh manner.

Verse No. 19

Here, on one side are those who believe in this and know that what is sent down from Allah is the truth, and in contrast to them are those who do not believe, who do not know; rather, those who stand opposite to them are blind. This is a very beautiful, impactful, and heart-settling manner of the Qur'an, in which it presents a person, a character, or a behavior in embodied form, and this image and parable is itself real, true, and without exaggeration. For example, the opponents are called blind here, and the truth is also that the person who does not see this clear and manifest reality, both outward and inward, can only be blind. Before this reality, people are of two kinds in relation to it. One group is the seeing group, and so it understands. The other is the group of the blind, and they are ignorant. Here, blindness does not mean blindness of the eyes, but blindness of the heart. It refers to the person whose faculties of perception have been extinguished, whose hearts have been sealed, whose spirit has been deprived of the fire of recognition, and in whose hearts even the last spark of knowledge of Allah has been extinguished.

"إنما يتذكر أولوا الألباب" (13:19) "Only people of understanding are the ones who accept admonition." Those people whose minds and hearts possess the faculty of perception, and who, when reminded of the truth, accept that reminder and admonition, and when the proofs of truth are presented before them, reflect upon them. The lofty and important attributes of ulu al-albab are these:

The Covenant of God is absolute: it includes every covenant that belongs to God, and the pledge (mithaq) is likewise absolute, meaning all the pledges made with God. The greatest covenant is the covenant of faith (iman), because all other covenants are its consequences and its requirements. The greatest pledge is that we will fulfil the demands of faith.

The covenant of faith is both ancient and new. The ancient covenant is the one bound to human nature (fitrah) and connected with the cosmic order (namus al-kainat), according to which this entire universe runs. Human nature directly perceives the single will by which this universe came into being, and is certain that the Creator of this universe is one, and that He alone deserves to be worshipped. This natural pledge is the one taken from all human beings while they were in the loins of Adam; in our view, this is the interpretation of the covenant of "Alast" (Am I not your Lord?) that we prefer, in its proper place. Then this covenant is renewed in the age of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), whom Allah sent to the nations not to take a new covenant, but so that he might remind them of this same covenant of "Alast" and explain and elucidate its meaning before the people. He tells people that the requirement of this covenant is that they worship Allah alone, cast off from their necks the yoke of worshipping everyone other than Allah, adopt righteous action and a firm commitment to the straight path, and in every matter turn to Allah alone, with whom humanity made the original covenant.

Within this great covenant of Allah are included the covenants that come after it, whether those covenants and pledges are with people, with messengers, with the common folk, with close relatives, with rulers, or with groups. Therefore, whoever is mindful of the first covenant and the first pledge will observe all other pledges, because fulfilling all covenants and pledges is an obligation. Whoever keeps the first covenant will also keep the other covenants, since all these covenants fall under it.

This is a great principle upon which the whole edifice of life is built. The Qur'an encapsulates this principle within a few words:

Verses 21 to 22

This is a general and comprehensive rule: that is, those who join the ties which Allah has commanded to be joined, who obey completely, remain fully faithful and steadfast. They walk straight according to the Sunnah of Allah, and there is no crookedness in their conduct. Therefore a comprehensive rule has been stated here, within which all the individual commands of Allah have come, since it would have been very difficult to mention all the commands one by one, and it was not even the purpose here. Rather, the purpose here was that a person should walk straight upon the demands of his fitrah (natural disposition) and be obedient in all matters, so that the bond of obedience is never broken. And at the end of the verse, a hint is also given that these people fear Allah and are very sensitive about perfect obedience.

﴿And they fear their Lord and dread that they may be called to a severe account﴾ (13:21). They fear the will of Allah and the severe reckoning of the Day of Resurrection, because they are wise, and a wise person prepares his account before the reckoning and accounting takes place.

﴿And those who patiently seek the Countenance of their Lord﴾ (13:22). Their condition is that they exercise patience for the pleasure of their Lord. Patience has many kinds and forms, and it has certain requirements. One patience is that a person be patient with difficulties on the path of the covenant he has made with Allah, such as difficulties in acts of worship, in jihad, and in the path of the Islamic call. Also patience in blessings, and patience in the hardships of life. Few are those who are patient in prosperity and do not become proud, arrogant, or ungrateful. Patience with the foolishness and ignorance of people, when often a person's patience is exhausted because of them. Likewise, patience in other matters and in the relationships of social life. All this patience is for the pleasure of Allah, not so that people may say that this person is courageous, or so that people may say that this person is complaining, nor merely to prove oneself noble, nor merely because lamentation and wailing will cause further loss. In short, patience performed for any purpose other than the pleasure of Allah is not accepted. Patience in blessings and in trials means that a person remains grateful and content with the decree of Allah.

﴿And establish prayer﴾ (13:22). Establishing prayer is also included in Allah's covenant and pledge, but it is mentioned separately here because it is the first sign and the pillar of fulfilling the covenant. Moreover, it is the important and clear manifestation of complete attention to Allah, and it is the physical link between the servant and the Lord. Prayer is purely for Allah; each of its movements and each of its words is for Allah and for Allah alone.

﴿And spend out of what We have provided them, secretly and openly﴾ (13:22). This command is also included in this verse, that they join the ties which Allah has commanded to be joined and fulfil the responsibilities and demands of the covenant with Allah. But it is brought here with special emphasis because it is the manifestation of social ties among the servants of Allah. Spending in the way of Allah strengthens the ties of divine and Islamic life. The heart of the giver is purified from the disease of miserliness, and the heart of the recipient is purified from rancour. The collective life of an Islamic society becomes based on mutual love and cooperation. Secret spending is in those situations where the dignity of the one receiving must be protected. Open spending is in those situations where there is a need to be an example for others, where the implementation of the Shariah is intended, or obedience to the law is intended, or some other collective benefit is intended.

﴿And they repel evil with good﴾ (13:22). The intended meaning here is that in daily affairs they repel evil through good. This does not refer to religious matters, where if someone does wrong, you should do good to him. Rather, the expression of the Qur'an here goes beyond the introduction and mentions the result. Answering evil with good causes the arrogance of a rebellious person to diminish, and a person is again inclined toward goodness in return for evil. The fire of evil is extinguished, and the whispers of Satan come to an end. Thus evil is averted and it disappears. Therefore the mention of good (hasanah) comes first in the verse.

Then, in this there is also an indication that repaying evil with good should be done only when there is hope that in this way evil will be averted and wrongdoing will end. But if a person becomes more arrogant because of it and grows bold, such an attitude will not be good. Rather, in such circumstances there will be a need to uproot evil from its root, and wherever defence is needed, evil will be resisted, so that the forces of evil do not forget and do not gain the boldness to adopt further rebellion.

Repaying evil with good is applied when the matter is between two individuals who are of equal standing. As for matters connected with the religion of Islam, it is not permissible to adopt this attitude, because in religious matters, for one who dares to transgress, only a naked sword cuts correctly. Furthermore, toward those whose habit is to spread corruption on the earth, a harsh attitude should be adopted. But what attitude should be taken in a given matter, the Qur'an has left such guidance to the discretion of the individual, that he should use his intellect to adopt the attitude in which there is goodness and betterment.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 13, verses 23–24:

Verses 23–24

For these people is the abode of the Hereafter. They will be of high station in the Hereafter. There will be gardens which will be eternal and everlasting for their dwelling. In such gardens their relatives and kin, their fathers and offspring, will also be with them, that is, those among them who are righteous. These people will enter those gardens on the basis of their own goodness and righteousness, but along with them their relatives will also enter as a mark of honour to them. Friends and companions will also be there. The gathering of friends and companions, and of fathers and offspring, is a beloved and delightful thing, which will double the pleasures of Paradise.

In this gathering, where friends and companions will be present and where relatives will be present, there will be messages of welcome (ahlan wa sahlan) and congratulation from the angels, and countless people will be coming and going there.

﴿Yadkhuluna 'alayhim min kulli bab﴾ (13:23): "They will enter upon them from every gate." Here the style of speech becomes such that it is as though we are watching this scene: from every direction the angels are coming in groups, and congratulations and peace are being conveyed.

﴿Salamun 'alaykum... al-dar﴾ (13:24): "Peace be upon you, for what you endured with patience in the world; how excellent is the final abode." It is as though it will be a festive gathering, and from every side there will be only joy, peace, blessing, and a stir of celebration and delight.

And on the other side will be those whose intellects were not functioning, so they could not take heed of admonition, nor did they have the insight to be patient over the hardships of the path of truth. The condition of these people will be, in every respect, the opposite of and contrary to the condition of the wise and thoughtful people.

Verse 25

They break the covenant of God after it has been firmly made, and they sever what God has commanded to be joined, and they cause corruption on the earth. For them there is a curse, and for them there is the evil abode.

This is the covenant of Alast which human nature made with God in the form of an eternal pledge, and after this they break every promise and agreement. If a person breaks the covenant of Alast, then he will be a violator of all the promises and covenants that rest upon that covenant of Alast. How can a person in whose heart there is no fear of God observe the trust of any person, any pledge, or any compact? That is to say, such people generally sever those ties which God has commanded to be joined.

As for the people of understanding and wisdom, they were patient, they established prayer, they spent in the way of God both openly and secretly, and their general conduct was to repay evil with good. But these people cause corruption on the earth. Abandoning any one of the qualities of the people of wisdom mentioned above gives rise to corruption on the earth.

"For them" — those who are far from God and cast out from His mercy — there is a curse. In contrast to honour and welcome there is rejection, and in contrast to the excellent abode there is the evil abode.

These people became cast out from God's mercy because they remained immersed in the enjoyments of the life of this world, and their gaze could not rise towards the eternal blessings of the Hereafter. Yet provision is determined solely in the hand of God; it is He who expands it and it is He who restricts it. All of this was within God's authority, and no person could provide for himself abundant sustenance such that he might become proud of it. Had these people been seekers of the Hereafter, it would not have been necessary for God to snatch away worldly prosperity from them, for He was the Giver.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 13, verse 26:

Verse No. 26

Earlier, a reference was made to this matter. A person who knows and accepts that the truth being revealed to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is the Truth is the one who is wise and intelligent, while the one who does not know it is blind. Now, here are some examples of the foolishness and blindness of the disbelievers, that these people are not able to see the signs and evidences of Allah in this universe. For people of understanding, the Qur'an alone is a sufficient miracle, but these people devoid of reason demand a miracle greater than the Qur'an itself. In the first part of the Surah, their demands were mentioned, and there it was also answered that the Messenger is only a warner, and the occurrence of miracles lies in the power of Allah. Here, such demands are repeated, and it is explained what the causes of misguidance and guidance are. Then, the hearts are mentioned that find tranquility only in the remembrance of Allah, and they do not demand further extraordinary miracles beyond this Qur'an and the Remembrance of Allah. This Qur'an, in its own place, possesses a profound power to influence, to the extent that on hearing it, the mountains are about to move, the earth is about to split apart, and the dead are about to raise slogans proclaiming its truth, because this Qur'an contains immense power, the substance of life, and a revolutionary spirit. Finally, the believers are guided not to despair of those who demand miracles, and to study the conduct of those people in human history who left good examples, and then to observe the condition of those who were like them and who were seized by the punishment of Allah.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 13, verses 27–32:

Verses 27 to 32

The summary of the refutation of these people is that the real cause of faith arising in hearts is not the occurrence of miracles. The callers to faith and the causes of faith exist within a person's own soul, and a person believes because of his own psychological states and innate inner impulses.

Qul inna Allah... unaab (13:27): "Say: Allah leads astray whom He wills, and guides to Himself whoever turns to Him in repentance."

Therefore Allah guides only those who have an inclination towards Him, and it is this inclination and this yearning for turning to Allah that made them believers. The second meaning of this is that those who have no inclination and no turning towards Allah are the ones who go astray, and so Allah also leads them astray. Therefore, guidance is attained through the capacity of hearts for guidance, then the seeking of guidance, and then striving on this path. But those hearts that are deprived even of the capacity for Allah's guidance, and that do not move in that direction at all, become distant from Allah and from guidance.

After this, a very pure portrait of believing hearts is drawn. This portrait is coloured with the hues of tranquillity and composure, intimacy and love, joy and cheerfulness.

Alladhina amanu wa tatma'innu qulubuhum bi-dhikr Allah (13:28): "Those who believed in the Prophet's call, their hearts find contentment in the remembrance of Allah." They have the feeling that they are connected with their Lord. They are within the embrace of Allah's mercy, and they are secure and protected with Allah. They are content even in the difficulties of loneliness and in the hardships of the path of truth. They are content with a clear understanding of the creation of the universe, its beginning and its end. They are content because they consider themselves under Allah's protection from every oppression, every evil and every transgression, except that if a calamity comes by the will of Allah, they are pleased with it too and, considering it a trial, they bear it with patience. They have complete trust in Allah regarding guidance, sustenance, and the concealing of their affairs in this world and the Hereafter, and therefore they are content.

Ala bi-dhikr Allah tatma'innu al-qulub (13:28): "Indeed, it is the remembrance of Allah by which hearts find tranquillity." The true knowledge of the tranquillity that arises in the hearts of believers is possessed only by those in whose hearts the sweetness and delight of faith have arisen and upon whom Allah's favour has descended. Such people perceive this delight and tranquillity of faith, but its states are of a kind that cannot be conveyed to others through words, especially to those who do not possess this recognition, because these realities lie beyond the grasp of words. This tranquillity penetrates the hearts; it gives them peace and joy, and gives them strength. They attain a sense of security and peace. Such people of knowledge feel that they are not alone; they find an entire environment as their friend and companion, because around them are Allah's artistry and creation, while the one who possesses this knowledge is himself under Allah's protection.

No one is more wretched on the face of this earth than those who are unaware of the love and intimacy that arise from their connection with Allah and from the remembrance of the Divine. There is no greater wretch than the one who wanders upon this earth without any intimacy or love for his cosmic surroundings. No one will be a greater wretch than the one who walks in this world and does not know what the purpose of his existence is, why he has come and where he is going, and why this burden of life has been placed upon him. And who would be more wretched than the one who walks upon this earth and shrinks from everything in his surroundings, though he knows there is a most subtle connection between him and everything? Who would be more wretched than the one who is travelling the journey of life yet is alone, cast out, lost, wandering alone among mountains and deserts, and traversing this arduous journey of life alone, without a guide, without a companion on the journey, and without a guide and helper, and does not even know the sign of his destination?

Be aware! In this arduous journey of life there come certain moments, very dark hours, which only one who has become Allah's can face, one who has the trust of Allah's support. Otherwise, however strong, brave and steadfast a person may be, there come dark hours in life when all of a person's powers fail. The final support is obtained only through the strength of connection with Allah and the remembrance of the Divine.

Ala bi-dhikr Allah tatma'innu al-qulub (13:28): "Beware! It is through the remembrance of Allah that hearts attain tranquillity." These people who turn towards Allah and are content through the remembrance of Allah will have a very good end with Allah, because they adopted good conduct and remained obedient to Allah.

Alladhina amanu... ma'ab (13:29): "Those who accepted the call to truth and did righteous deeds, for them is blessedness and a good place of return." Tuba is from taba, yatibu, on the pattern of kubra. This form is used for magnification and honour, meaning that for them there is a very great good news. Their good end will be with the God whose obedient servants they remained in their lives.

Those who demand miracles do not have the awareness of faith and tranquillity. They are afflicted with mental disquiet, and to remove this mental anxiety they demand miracles. O Prophet, you are not the first Messenger to come to a people, that this matter has become incomprehensible to these people. Many nations have passed before, and many messengers have passed. If these people have become set upon disbelief, then you continue working according to your method and place your trust in Allah.

Kadhalika arsalnaka... matab (13:30): "O Prophet, in this very manner We sent you as a Messenger, to a people before whom many nations have passed away, so that you might recite to them the message which We have revealed to you, while they are disbelieving in the Most Gracious God. Say: He is my Lord; there is no god but He. In Him I have placed my trust, and to Him is my return." It is strange that these people disbelieve in the Most Merciful, whose mercy is very great, through whose remembrance hearts find tranquillity, and in whom the awareness of His great mercy arises. O Prophet, your duty is only that you recite to these people the revelation that comes to you; this is the very purpose of your sending. If they have become set upon committing disbelief, then declare that my trust is solely in Allah, the One, and that I am returning to Him, and that I have no need to turn to anyone else for refuge.

We have given you only the duty of conveying the call of the Quran to people. Recite the Quran; this Book and this speech in itself contains great wonders. If mountains were set in motion by means of any Quran, or the earth were cleft into pieces, or the dead were made to speak through it, these matters would be present in this Quran and these mentioned miracles would manifest through it. But the Quran (and every Divine Book) is revealed so that the common people may be informed of their duties and their obligations. If these addressees have now become set upon disbelief and absolutely refuse to believe, then the time has come for the believers to despair of them and leave them, so that what Allah does with the deniers may come upon them.

Wa law anna qur'anan... al-mi'ad (13:31): "What would have happened if a Quran had been sent down by which mountains would be moved, or the earth would be split, or the dead would rise from their graves and speak? (Showing such signs is not difficult.) Rather, all authority is in the hands of Allah. Have not the believers, while hoping for some sign in response to the demands of the disbelievers, despaired on realising that if Allah had willed, He would have guided all mankind? Those who have adopted an attitude of disbelief towards God are afflicted, because of their deeds, by some calamity that keeps coming, or it descends close to their homes. This process will continue until the promise of Allah comes to pass. Surely Allah does not break His promise."

The truth is that those who accepted the Quran and immersed themselves in its states were so transformed by it that, compared to it, the moving of mountains, the splitting of the earth and the raising of the dead would be a great miracle. The miracles mentioned also brought far-reaching changes to the lives of those people, and great miracles took place. The values of their lives were changed; indeed, Islam and the Muslims themselves changed the very face of this earth, and Islam and the Muslims changed the course of the history of this globe.

The effectiveness of this Quran, its essence and style, its call and philosophy, its subjects of discourse and its manner of expression, is in itself a great miracle. It has a great influence against any miracle, however great. And only the one who is acquainted with its sublime qualities, its philosophies, its modes of expression and its styles of speech, and who possesses the intellectual faculty to comprehend these things, is aware of this miraculous character. Those who understood it, acted upon it, and were immersed in its states and its lights, performed miracles greater than the moving of mountains. Through the effects of the Quran, the conditions of nations and generations and the currents of their thinking were transformed. They shattered things that were harder than the earth. The intellectual stagnation and the stagnation of customs and traditions which the Quran and the Muslims broke were far harder than earth and stones. They brought to life nations that were more dead than the dead, nations that, though alive, were dead, whose spirit had been killed by illusion and conjecture. They were worshippers of the idols of illusion and conjecture. The revolution that took place among the Arabs, the change that appeared in their lives, and about which there is no room for doubt, that this revolution came solely and exclusively through the Quran, which completely transformed the way of their lives, is it not a revolution no less than the moving of mountains, the splitting of the earth and the dead speaking?

Bal lillahi al-amru jami'an (13:31): "Rather, all authority belongs to Allah." It is He who determines the nature of the movement, and He who chooses the means and instruments for the movement. If, on hearing this Quran, some people's hearts are still not stirred and roused, then it is appropriate for the believers, who are still striving to stir such hearts, to despair of such people and leave their matter to Allah. Had Allah willed, He would have placed in all people the capacity for guidance, and created human beings with an instinct for guidance just as He created the angels upon guidance. Or He would have compelled people and set them upon the path of guidance. But Allah has neither devised a plan of good for human beings nor given them an angelic instinct, because Allah created man for a specific purpose, and Allah knew how man could fulfil the requirements of that purpose.

Therefore, people should now be left to Allah's decisions. If Allah has decided that He will not destroy these Arab peoples in the way that He destroyed some nations, then some calamity keeps coming upon them, or comes close to their homes, and these people from time to time become victims of Allah's punishments, and some of them even perish in these afflictions.

Aw tahullu qariban min darihim (13:31): "Or it descends close to their homes." By which they become fearful, and then they wait with great anxiety and fear, lest a calamity like it come again. Some people also become softened; a movement arises among them, and they receive real life.

Hatta ya'tiya wa'd Allah (13:31): "Surely Allah does not break His promise." It is Allah's promise that the Hour is coming, there is no doubt about it, and every person on that day will face the outcome that Allah has promised. Examples of this exist in human history: Allah grants respite, but after respite and waiting, Allah's grip also comes.

Wa laqad istuhzi'a... 'iqab (13:32): "Messengers before you were also mocked, but I gave respite to the deniers, then I seized them; so see how severe was My punishment." This is a question for which there is no need of an answer. That punishment was such that generations continued to speak of it.

The second matter is that of the partners (shuraka'). It was touched upon in the first part of the Surah as well. Here too these wretched ones are mentioned in a manner of utter contempt. Their comparison with Allah is made in such a way that Allah is established over every soul; He recompenses every person for his deeds in this world as well, and those who attribute to Allah the falsehood that He has partners are punished in this world, and are punished in the Hereafter too, and the Hereafter is most severe, whereas security and peace await the people of piety.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 13, verses 27–32:

Verses 27 to 32

The summary of the refutation of these people is that the real cause of faith arising in hearts is not the occurrence of miracles. The callers to faith and the causes of faith exist within a person's own soul, and a person believes because of his own psychological states and innate inner impulses.

Qul inna Allah... unaab (13:27): "Say: Allah leads astray whom He wills, and guides to Himself whoever turns to Him in repentance."

Therefore Allah guides only those who have an inclination towards Him, and it is this inclination and this yearning for turning to Allah that made them believers. The second meaning of this is that those who have no inclination and no turning towards Allah are the ones who go astray, and so Allah also leads them astray. Therefore, guidance is attained through the capacity of hearts for guidance, then the seeking of guidance, and then striving on this path. But those hearts that are deprived even of the capacity for Allah's guidance, and that do not move in that direction at all, become distant from Allah and from guidance.

After this, a very pure portrait of believing hearts is drawn. This portrait is coloured with the hues of tranquillity and composure, intimacy and love, joy and cheerfulness.

Alladhina amanu wa tatma'innu qulubuhum bi-dhikr Allah (13:28): "Those who believed in the Prophet's call, their hearts find contentment in the remembrance of Allah." They have the feeling that they are connected with their Lord. They are within the embrace of Allah's mercy, and they are secure and protected with Allah. They are content even in the difficulties of loneliness and in the hardships of the path of truth. They are content with a clear understanding of the creation of the universe, its beginning and its end. They are content because they consider themselves under Allah's protection from every oppression, every evil and every transgression, except that if a calamity comes by the will of Allah, they are pleased with it too and, considering it a trial, they bear it with patience. They have complete trust in Allah regarding guidance, sustenance, and the concealing of their affairs in this world and the Hereafter, and therefore they are content.

Ala bi-dhikr Allah tatma'innu al-qulub (13:28): "Indeed, it is the remembrance of Allah by which hearts find tranquillity." The true knowledge of the tranquillity that arises in the hearts of believers is possessed only by those in whose hearts the sweetness and delight of faith have arisen and upon whom Allah's favour has descended. Such people perceive this delight and tranquillity of faith, but its states are of a kind that cannot be conveyed to others through words, especially to those who do not possess this recognition, because these realities lie beyond the grasp of words. This tranquillity penetrates the hearts; it gives them peace and joy, and gives them strength. They attain a sense of security and peace. Such people of knowledge feel that they are not alone; they find an entire environment as their friend and companion, because around them are Allah's artistry and creation, while the one who possesses this knowledge is himself under Allah's protection.

No one is more wretched on the face of this earth than those who are unaware of the love and intimacy that arise from their connection with Allah and from the remembrance of the Divine. There is no greater wretch than the one who wanders upon this earth without any intimacy or love for his cosmic surroundings. No one will be a greater wretch than the one who walks in this world and does not know what the purpose of his existence is, why he has come and where he is going, and why this burden of life has been placed upon him. And who would be more wretched than the one who walks upon this earth and shrinks from everything in his surroundings, though he knows there is a most subtle connection between him and everything? Who would be more wretched than the one who is travelling the journey of life yet is alone, cast out, lost, wandering alone among mountains and deserts, and traversing this arduous journey of life alone, without a guide, without a companion on the journey, and without a guide and helper, and does not even know the sign of his destination?

Be aware! In this arduous journey of life there come certain moments, very dark hours, which only one who has become Allah's can face, one who has the trust of Allah's support. Otherwise, however strong, brave and steadfast a person may be, there come dark hours in life when all of a person's powers fail. The final support is obtained only through the strength of connection with Allah and the remembrance of the Divine.

Ala bi-dhikr Allah tatma'innu al-qulub (13:28): "Beware! It is through the remembrance of Allah that hearts attain tranquillity." These people who turn towards Allah and are content through the remembrance of Allah will have a very good end with Allah, because they adopted good conduct and remained obedient to Allah.

Alladhina amanu... ma'ab (13:29): "Those who accepted the call to truth and did righteous deeds, for them is blessedness and a good place of return." Tuba is from taba, yatibu, on the pattern of kubra. This form is used for magnification and honour, meaning that for them there is a very great good news. Their good end will be with the God whose obedient servants they remained in their lives.

Those who demand miracles do not have the awareness of faith and tranquillity. They are afflicted with mental disquiet, and to remove this mental anxiety they demand miracles. O Prophet, you are not the first Messenger to come to a people, that this matter has become incomprehensible to these people. Many nations have passed before, and many messengers have passed. If these people have become set upon disbelief, then you continue working according to your method and place your trust in Allah.

Kadhalika arsalnaka... matab (13:30): "O Prophet, in this very manner We sent you as a Messenger, to a people before whom many nations have passed away, so that you might recite to them the message which We have revealed to you, while they are disbelieving in the Most Gracious God. Say: He is my Lord; there is no god but He. In Him I have placed my trust, and to Him is my return." It is strange that these people disbelieve in the Most Merciful, whose mercy is very great, through whose remembrance hearts find tranquillity, and in whom the awareness of His great mercy arises. O Prophet, your duty is only that you recite to these people the revelation that comes to you; this is the very purpose of your sending. If they have become set upon committing disbelief, then declare that my trust is solely in Allah, the One, and that I am returning to Him, and that I have no need to turn to anyone else for refuge.

We have given you only the duty of conveying the call of the Quran to people. Recite the Quran; this Book and this speech in itself contains great wonders. If mountains were set in motion by means of any Quran, or the earth were cleft into pieces, or the dead were made to speak through it, these matters would be present in this Quran and these mentioned miracles would manifest through it. But the Quran (and every Divine Book) is revealed so that the common people may be informed of their duties and their obligations. If these addressees have now become set upon disbelief and absolutely refuse to believe, then the time has come for the believers to despair of them and leave them, so that what Allah does with the deniers may come upon them.

Wa law anna qur'anan... al-mi'ad (13:31): "What would have happened if a Quran had been sent down by which mountains would be moved, or the earth would be split, or the dead would rise from their graves and speak? (Showing such signs is not difficult.) Rather, all authority is in the hands of Allah. Have not the believers, while hoping for some sign in response to the demands of the disbelievers, despaired on realising that if Allah had willed, He would have guided all mankind? Those who have adopted an attitude of disbelief towards God are afflicted, because of their deeds, by some calamity that keeps coming, or it descends close to their homes. This process will continue until the promise of Allah comes to pass. Surely Allah does not break His promise."

The truth is that those who accepted the Quran and immersed themselves in its states were so transformed by it that, compared to it, the moving of mountains, the splitting of the earth and the raising of the dead would be a great miracle. The miracles mentioned also brought far-reaching changes to the lives of those people, and great miracles took place. The values of their lives were changed; indeed, Islam and the Muslims themselves changed the very face of this earth, and Islam and the Muslims changed the course of the history of this globe.

The effectiveness of this Quran, its essence and style, its call and philosophy, its subjects of discourse and its manner of expression, is in itself a great miracle. It has a great influence against any miracle, however great. And only the one who is acquainted with its sublime qualities, its philosophies, its modes of expression and its styles of speech, and who possesses the intellectual faculty to comprehend these things, is aware of this miraculous character. Those who understood it, acted upon it, and were immersed in its states and its lights, performed miracles greater than the moving of mountains. Through the effects of the Quran, the conditions of nations and generations and the currents of their thinking were transformed. They shattered things that were harder than the earth. The intellectual stagnation and the stagnation of customs and traditions which the Quran and the Muslims broke were far harder than earth and stones. They brought to life nations that were more dead than the dead, nations that, though alive, were dead, whose spirit had been killed by illusion and conjecture. They were worshippers of the idols of illusion and conjecture. The revolution that took place among the Arabs, the change that appeared in their lives, and about which there is no room for doubt, that this revolution came solely and exclusively through the Quran, which completely transformed the way of their lives, is it not a revolution no less than the moving of mountains, the splitting of the earth and the dead speaking?

Bal lillahi al-amru jami'an (13:31): "Rather, all authority belongs to Allah." It is He who determines the nature of the movement, and He who chooses the means and instruments for the movement. If, on hearing this Quran, some people's hearts are still not stirred and roused, then it is appropriate for the believers, who are still striving to stir such hearts, to despair of such people and leave their matter to Allah. Had Allah willed, He would have placed in all people the capacity for guidance, and created human beings with an instinct for guidance just as He created the angels upon guidance. Or He would have compelled people and set them upon the path of guidance. But Allah has neither devised a plan of good for human beings nor given them an angelic instinct, because Allah created man for a specific purpose, and Allah knew how man could fulfil the requirements of that purpose.

Therefore, people should now be left to Allah's decisions. If Allah has decided that He will not destroy these Arab peoples in the way that He destroyed some nations, then some calamity keeps coming upon them, or comes close to their homes, and these people from time to time become victims of Allah's punishments, and some of them even perish in these afflictions.

Aw tahullu qariban min darihim (13:31): "Or it descends close to their homes." By which they become fearful, and then they wait with great anxiety and fear, lest a calamity like it come again. Some people also become softened; a movement arises among them, and they receive real life.

Hatta ya'tiya wa'd Allah (13:31): "Surely Allah does not break His promise." It is Allah's promise that the Hour is coming, there is no doubt about it, and every person on that day will face the outcome that Allah has promised. Examples of this exist in human history: Allah grants respite, but after respite and waiting, Allah's grip also comes.

Wa laqad istuhzi'a... 'iqab (13:32): "Messengers before you were also mocked, but I gave respite to the deniers, then I seized them; so see how severe was My punishment." This is a question for which there is no need of an answer. That punishment was such that generations continued to speak of it.

The second matter is that of the partners (shuraka'). It was touched upon in the first part of the Surah as well. Here too these wretched ones are mentioned in a manner of utter contempt. Their comparison with Allah is made in such a way that Allah is established over every soul; He recompenses every person for his deeds in this world as well, and those who attribute to Allah the falsehood that He has partners are punished in this world, and are punished in the Hereafter too, and the Hereafter is most severe, whereas security and peace await the people of piety.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 13, verses 33–36:

Verses 33 to 35

Allah, glorified and exalted, is Watchful over every soul. In every state, every living being is within Allah's power. Allah knows what each one is doing, whether openly or in secret. However, the manner of the Qur'an's expression is such that it presents this watchfulness and control in a very concrete form. This is the Qur'an's manner of speech: it presents meanings and concepts in a concrete form, so that the listener, affected by it, begins to tremble.

﴿Then is He who stands over every soul in what it has earned...﴾ (13:33). Every person should imagine that above him stands a watcher, who sees him and takes account of him. Who? Allah. Now, who is there who does not tremble with fear when this concept is held to be the reality of things? The Qur'an presents this spiritual meaning before the perceptive faculties of man in a very sensory manner, because man is more affected by perceptible scenes than by abstract meanings.

When the situation is like this, do they still ascribe partners to Allah? In the light of this scene, the conduct of these people appears extremely repugnant and abominable. Anyone who sees this scene begins to wonder at the attitude of such people.

﴿And they have set up for Allah partners...﴾ (13:33). Although Allah is Watchful over every soul, and the earnings of every person are before His sight, nothing can escape Allah.

﴿Say: Name them...﴾ (13:33). Because the names that are mentioned for these partners are mere names. It is possible that some idols and partners do have names, but the manner of expression, in a tone of command and contempt, asks as though regarding them as unknown entities: just tell us their real names.

﴿Or do you inform Him of something He does not know in the earth?﴾ (13:33). This is a mockery of them: that you, being humans, possess information of which Allah has no knowledge in His dominion. What a strange thought this is of yours! You know that there are other gods besides Allah, and Allah is unaware of it? Even the disbelievers did not dare to make such a claim, but by the tongue of their state their claim was exactly this: Allah was proclaiming aloud that there is no god but Him, while these people said that so-and-so is also a god.

﴿Or is it [just] an outward saying?﴾ (13:33). You people make statements about the existence of other deities as a mere superficial matter, and such words have no meaning or significance, whereas the question of divinity is not a matter to be decided by superficial talk, as if the issues of divinity, monotheism and polytheism could be resolved through idle chatter.

Up to here it was a mocking response. Now the matter is discussed seriously.

﴿Rather, the plotting of those who disbelieved has been made attractive to them...﴾ (13:33). The matter is this: these people disbelieved, concealed from themselves the proofs of faith, and kept their hearts and minds veiled from the proofs of faith and guidance. Therefore the divine way (sunnah) applied to them in truth. Their own selves persuaded them that they were upon the truth, and made them believe that their schemes and their plans against the truth were very good and successful. Thus this conduct of theirs kept them away from the path of truth. The one whom Allah, under His laws of guidance and misguidance, declares to be misguided, for him there can be no guide. For when an individual or a people provides the causes of the divine laws, then Allah's sunnah becomes unalterable.

And what is the end of such people?

﴿For them is a punishment in the life of this world...﴾ (13:34). For such people there is punishment in this worldly life. If a calamity befalls them, or a calamity descends near their homes, it is still a punishment for them, since these people will always remain in fear and anxiety that this very calamity is about to fall upon them. Moreover, if someone's heart becomes dry for faith and turns to stone, is that a small punishment, when such faithless hearts remain constantly in bewilderment, distress and restlessness? Misfortunes keep befalling them, yet they do not understand why this punishment has come upon them.

﴿And the punishment of the Hereafter is harsher...﴾ (13:34). Here the details of the severities of the punishment of the Hereafter are not given, so that a person may think about it himself.

﴿And they will have no protector from Allah...﴾ (13:34). No one can save them from Allah, to rescue them from Allah's seizure and protect them from Allah's punishment. Whatever punishment comes upon them, they will continue to endure it.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 13, verses 37–40:

Now the discussion moves forward with the themes of revelation and tawhid. It is explained what the position of the People of the Book is regarding the Qur'an and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). It is stated that the instructions given in the earlier scriptures have now been made subject to this final Book. Its command is decisive (qawl fasl) and it is the final and conclusive ruling. In this final Book, Allah has given commands that will remain valid until the Last Day. Among them are matters that were revealed to the earlier messengers. Moreover, through this Book Allah has erased those parts of the earlier scriptures that He deemed fit to erase. Only Allah knows the wisdom behind them. Therefore, O Prophet, hold firmly to the position that is the position of the Qur'an, and do not follow the desires of the people, especially the People of the Book, neither in a minor matter nor in a major one. As for those who demand miracles, tell them plainly that your duty is to convey the message. When a miracle is needed, its appearance and occurrence take place by the permission of Allah.

Verses 36 to 40

Among the People of the Book, those who are truthful and who adhere to the fundamental teachings of the religion of Jesus, when they read the Qur'an, find the teachings of the Qur'an in harmony with their own fundamental teachings, for example in the belief in tawhid and so on. Moreover, they see that the Qur'an accepts the truth of all heavenly religions and all heavenly scriptures, mentions them all with great respect, and gives the impression that all believers, whether they are believers in the final Prophet or believers in the earlier prophets, are one community and one nation, and the Divine Being is their commander. Such people rejoice greatly and believe. Here the inner state of such people is described as joy (farah), because when a person finds the truth, he feels great happiness, and when they find their own ideas confirmed in the Qur'an, their conviction becomes even firmer, and by believing in the Qur'an they become supporters of this movement.

"And among the factions there are those who deny part of it" (13:36). That is, by them are meant some groups among the People of the Book and the polytheists. The details of these people are not given here, because the purpose is only to mention the deniers and refute them.

"Say: I have only been commanded to worship Allah and not to associate anything with Him. So I call to Him, and to Him is my return" (13:36). That is, worship is for Him alone, the call is to Allah, and the return is to Allah alone.

The Messenger (ﷺ) is commanded to make his position clear to those who deny some of the teachings of the Qur'an: that he will firmly hold the entire Book that has been revealed to him, whether the People of the Book are pleased or some of them are displeased, because what has been revealed to him is the final ruling. The earlier rulings have been abrogated, this Book has been revealed in the Arabic language, and its meaning is also clear and complete, because now it is Allah's final message. Therefore, we now derive all our principles from it.

"And thus We have sent it down as an Arabic judgment" (13:37).

"And if you were to follow their desires after the knowledge that has come to you, you would have no protector or helper against Allah" (13:37). Because the knowledge that is coming to you is certain knowledge, whereas what the other groups say are their own desires, not based on knowledge and certainty. This command is given to the Messenger (ﷺ) in threatening terms, and this manner is a more eloquent way of fixing this truth in the mind. The purpose is that there is no room for any compromise in this matter, not even for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), though it is inconceivable that the Messenger would do so.

If someone objects that the Prophet (ﷺ) is a human being, he should know that all messengers were human beings.

"And We certainly sent messengers before you and gave them wives and offspring" (13:38).

And if the objection is that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not come with a material miracle, he should know that this is not his task; it is the task of Allah.

"And it was not for any messenger to bring a sign except by permission of Allah" (13:38). Allah, according to His wisdom, causes extraordinary miracles to occur where they are needed.

Yes, there is indeed a difference in some details between the Books given to the People of the Book and the Book given to the final Prophet, because each era has its own Book. But this is the final Book.

"For every term is a decree. Allah erases what He wills and establishes [what He wills], and with Him is the Mother of the Book" (13:38–39). When the wisdom of Allah requires it, He erases whatever command He wills and keeps in place what is beneficial. The original Book and the plan of all matters is preserved with Him, containing all the details of this erasure, abrogation, and new rulings. Therefore, all scriptures belong to Him; He alters and abrogates in them wherever and whenever His wisdom requires. No one can reject His will, and no one has the right to object.

Now, the punishment with which Allah has threatened these people, and the evil end they will face, whether they meet it while the Messenger (ﷺ) is present or the Messenger passes away before it, makes no difference to their fate. Nor does it make any difference to the Messenger's prophethood or to the divinity of the Lord, the Exalted.

"And whether We show you part of what We promise them or We take you away, your duty is only to convey, and upon Us is the reckoning" (13:40).

In this decisive guidance there is insight for the nature of the Islamic movement and for its leadership. The duty of the leadership is only to adopt a suitable policy at every stage and to carry out its obligation. It is not their duty to bring the movement to the end to which Allah intends to bring it. Nor is it their duty to show haste in the movement's stages and steps, nor to become despondent by announcing the failure of the movement. When the leadership sees that Allah's decision is delayed, and that they have not been granted authority in the land, and that they are still far from power, they should not be distressed; they are only callers, merely callers.

The signs of Allah's power are visible in your environment. Allah seizes mighty and strong nations. They fall into the pit of decline when they act arrogantly on earth and spread corruption. The strength of such nations diminishes, their wealth diminishes, and their importance steadily declines. At one time the sun never set on their rule, but later they shrink and are reduced; and when Allah decrees the defeat and loss of a people, there is no one to question Allah, and Allah's decision is carried out without fail.

Here the inner state of such people is described as joy (farah), because when a person finds the truth, he feels great happiness, and when they find their own ideas confirmed in the Qur'an, their conviction becomes even firmer, and by believing in the Qur'an they become supporters of this movement.

"And among the factions there are those who deny part of it" (13:36). That is, by them are meant some groups among the People of the Book and the polytheists. The details of these people are not given here, because the purpose is only to mention the deniers and refute them.

"Say: I have only been commanded to worship Allah and not to associate anything with Him. So I call to Him, and to Him is my return" (13:36). That is, worship is for Him alone, the call is to Allah, and the return is to Allah alone.

The Messenger (ﷺ) is commanded to make his position clear to those who deny some of the teachings of the Qur'an: that he will firmly hold the entire Book that has been revealed to him, whether the People of the Book are pleased or some of them are displeased, because what has been revealed to him is the final ruling. The earlier rulings have been abrogated, this Book has been revealed in the Arabic language, and its meaning is also clear and complete, because now it is Allah's final message. Therefore, we now derive all our principles from it.

"And thus We have sent it down as an Arabic judgment" (13:37).

"And if you were to follow their desires after the knowledge that has come to you, you would have no protector or helper against Allah" (13:37). Because the knowledge that is coming to you is certain knowledge, whereas what the other groups say are their own desires, not based on knowledge and certainty. This command is given to the Messenger (ﷺ) in threatening terms, and this manner is a more eloquent way of fixing this truth in the mind. The purpose is that there is no room for any compromise in this matter, not even for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), though it is inconceivable that the Messenger would do so.

If someone objects that the Prophet (ﷺ) is a human being, he should know that all messengers were human beings.

"And We certainly sent messengers before you and gave them wives and offspring" (13:38).

And if the objection is that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not come with a material miracle, he should know that this is not his task; it is the task of Allah.

"And it was not for any messenger to bring a sign except by permission of Allah" (13:38). Allah, according to His wisdom, causes extraordinary miracles to occur where they are needed.

Yes, there is indeed a difference in some details between the Books given to the People of the Book and the Book given to the final Prophet, because each era has its own Book. But this is the final Book.

"For every term is a decree. Allah erases what He wills and establishes [what He wills], and with Him is the Mother of the Book" (13:38–39). When the wisdom of Allah requires it, He erases whatever command He wills and keeps in place what is beneficial. The original Book and the plan of all matters is preserved with Him, containing all the details of this erasure, abrogation, and new rulings. Therefore, all scriptures belong to Him; He alters and abrogates in them wherever and whenever His wisdom requires. No one can reject His will, and no one has the right to object.

Now, the punishment with which Allah has threatened these people, and the evil end they will face, whether they meet it while the Messenger (ﷺ) is present or the Messenger passes away before it, makes no difference to their fate. Nor does it make any difference to the Messenger's prophethood or to the divinity of the Lord, the Exalted.

"And whether We show you part of what We promise them or We take you away, your duty is only to convey, and upon Us is the reckoning" (13:40).

In this decisive guidance there is insight for the nature of the Islamic movement and for its leadership. The duty of the leadership is only to adopt a suitable policy at every stage and to carry out its obligation. It is not their duty to bring the movement to the end to which Allah intends to bring it. Nor is it their duty to show haste in the movement's stages and steps, nor to become despondent by announcing the failure of the movement. When the leadership sees that Allah's decision is delayed, and that they have not been granted authority in the land, and that they are still far from power, they should not be distressed; they are only callers, merely callers.

The signs of Allah's power are visible in your environment. Allah seizes mighty and strong nations. They fall into the pit of decline when they act arrogantly on earth and spread corruption. The strength of such nations diminishes, their wealth diminishes, and their importance steadily declines. At one time the sun never set on their rule, but later they shrink and are reduced; and when Allah decrees the defeat and loss of a people, there is no one to question Allah, and Allah's decision is carried out without fail.
