Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 13, verse 43 (part 1 of 3):

Verse No. 43

This surah concludes. It has taken the human heart on a tour of the whole universe and also made it wander through the world of the human self, leaving deep and far-reaching effects upon it, and then it has brought the believing heart to the proof that Allah is a witness to what the Qur'an says. This testimony of Allah is brought at the beginning of the surah and also at its conclusion. After the testimony of Allah, what other evidence would be needed to prove a claim? With the testimony of Allah, the matter is settled.

At the conclusion of this surah it is necessary to say that in this surah the Islamic outlook on life and the method (manhaj) by which the Qur'an presents this outlook must be considered. The right course would have been to give this detail right where the verses describing it appear, but we did not think it appropriate to interrupt the flow of the verses by introducing a detailed discussion in the middle of the exegesis of the verses. Therefore we thought it appropriate to postpone this topic until the end of the surah.

We have, in any case, made allusions to the Islamic outlook on life and its method in the course of the commentary on the verses. Here, after the conclusion of the surah, it is now appropriate to present the matter in somewhat more detail. wa-Allahu al-musta'an!

The opening of this surah, its subjects, and most of the guidance given within it show that this surah is Meccan. As some narrations say it is Madani, in truth it is not Madani. Likewise, as some copies of the Qur'an (masahif) also write it as Madani, the evidence of those (who hold otherwise) shows that this surah was revealed in that period of Mecca in which the people were strongly turning away from the Islamic call. They were denying it, and even challenging the Islamic call. For example, this surah shows that the polytheists repeatedly demanded miracles, and demanded why the punishment with which they were being warned did not descend upon them quickly. Therefore there was a need for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his handful of companions to be advised that they should not be distressed, and should remain firm upon the truth on which they stood. The call they have is a lofty call, so through it they should confront this aversion, denial and challenge, and should only pray to Allah that He remove their difficulties, and should openly declare that Allah alone is the Sovereign, Creator and Lord, and should remain firm on this position and hold the belief that this is the truth, even if the polytheists deny it. This surah also presents to the polytheists the proofs which are scattered throughout this universe, and the proofs which are within their own selves, and then those in the history of humanity and its important events. In short, these and countless other kinds of proofs are presented in this surah in a most effective manner, whose effects penetrate deeply into the heart and from which human thought receives much nourishment.

For example, this surah states that this Book alone is the truth and that this is the reality, even if people turn away from it, deny it, challenge it, and delay in accepting it. The difficulties on this path are not a proof that this Book is not true.

Al-Mar. Tilka... yu'minun (13:1): "These are the verses of the Book, and what has been sent down to you from your Lord is the very truth, but most people do not believe."

Kadhalika yadribu Allahu... al-amthal (13:17): "In this manner Allah illustrates the matter of truth and falsehood: as for the foam, it passes away, and as for that which benefits people, it remains upon the earth. Thus Allah explains matters through parables."

Afaman ya'lamu... ulu al-albab (13:19): "Can it be that one who knows that what has been sent down to you from your Lord is the truth is equal to one who is blind to this reality? Only people of understanding accept admonition."

Wa-yaqulu alladhina... tatma'innu al-qulub (13:27-28): "Those who have disbelieved (in the message of Muhammad) say: 'Why is no sign sent down upon him from his Lord?' Say: 'Allah leads astray whom He wills, and guides to Himself the one who turns to Him.' Those are the ones who have believed (in the Islamic call), and the hearts of such people find peace in the remembrance of Allah."

Kadhalika arsalnaka... wa-ilayhi mata (13:30): "O Prophet, in this same manner We have sent you as a messenger to a people before whom many nations have passed, so that you may recite to them what We have revealed to you, while they are disbelieving in the Most Merciful. Say: 'He is my Lord; there is no god but Him. In Him I have placed my trust, and to Him is my return.'"

Wa-alladhina ataynahumu... min waliyin wa-la waqin (13:36-37): "O Prophet, those to whom We gave the Book before are pleased with what We have sent down to you, and among the various groups there are some who reject part of it. Say plainly: 'I have only been commanded to worship Allah and not to associate anything with Him. So I call to Him alone, and to Him is my return.' Upon this guidance We have sent down this Arabic command to you. Now, if you follow the desires of the people after the knowledge that has come to you, then you will have neither a supporter nor a protector against Allah, and no one can save you from His seizure."

Wa-in ma nurinnaka... al-hisab (13:40): "And O Prophet, whether We show you some part of the evil end with which We threaten these people, or We take you away before its occurrence, your duty is only to convey the message, and the reckoning is Our responsibility."

Wa-yaqulu alladhina... 'ilm al-kitab (13:43): "The deniers say: 'You are not sent by Allah.' Say: 'Sufficient is Allah's testimony between me and you, and also the one who has knowledge of the Book.'"

Reflect on these verses; from them it is felt how the polytheists of Mecca were opposing and resisting the person of the Prophet ﷺ and this Qur'an, and in these circumstances what attitude Allah and the Qur'an commanded them to adopt regarding this harsh stance of the polytheists of Mecca.

What is clearly and plainly stated in these verses is that, in contrast to this polytheistic policy of turning away, denying, resisting, accepting the call very slowly, and placing immense difficulties in the way of the call, Allah gave clear guidance to the Messenger ﷺ that he should speak to them frankly and openly declare the truth revealed to him. The basic points of the Islamic call are that there is no deity or creator except Allah, there is no sovereign or lawgiver except Him, there is none worthy of worship and obedience except Him, He is the One and the Subduer, and all people will return to Him, either to Paradise or to Fire. These were the very points which the polytheists of Mecca denied and resisted. The Messenger ﷺ was told not to seek the pleasure of these polytheists by concealing some of this truth or by delaying its proclamation. In this regard, the Messenger ﷺ was given an open threat: if he sought to gain their pleasure, there would also be punishment for him with Allah, and no one could save him.

This clear allusion, indeed proclamation, clearly tells those who call to Allah that this is the method of this call, and that there is no need for any ijtihad in it, nor any need to adopt a special strategy. Callers should declare the basic points of this call openly and clearly. They should omit none of these points, nor postpone any of them. The first of these basic truths and points is that since the Deity, Sovereign, Lord and Lawgiver is Allah alone, obedience cannot be rendered to anyone or any will other than Allah. Whatever the circumstances, however powerful and harsh the opposing forces may be, the declaration of this point is necessary, even if people do not accept it, turn away from it, or difficulties with the greatest severity stand in the way, and the situations are most dangerous. It is neither within wisdom (hikmah) nor within good admonition (maw'izah hasanah) that some points of the Islamic call be hidden or postponed merely because the satanic (taghuti) forces within the country do not like it, or because they inflict violence upon workers, turn away, or conspire against the callers. For, on account of these reasons, it is not permissible for the callers of truth to abandon or postpone any of these fundamental points of Islam. It is not permissible for the callers of truth to adopt such symbols, morals and manners, or to take the path of spiritual and moral reform, while abandoning the clear proclamation of Allah's oneness and sovereignty, and consequently to abandon the call to obedience to the Islamic system merely so as to escape the wrath and vengeance of those satanic forces.

Let it be remembered that Allah has indicated that this method, and this alone, is the method for presenting the Islamic outlook on life, and it is this method upon which Muhammad ﷺ walked throughout his entire life in accordance with Allah's command. Moreover, it is not permissible for any caller coming after him to abandon this method of Muhammad ﷺ or to adopt any other method. Allah Himself is responsible for the protection of His religion. He is also responsible for the protection of His callers, and He is the one who deals with the intrigues of the rebellious.

In the style of calling to Islam which the Qur'an has adopted, there are both the commands, guidance and proofs which Allah has sent down in His Book, and the proofs, evidences and indications which are present and observable in the open book of this universe. The Qur'an makes this entire universe a subject for reflection for the human personality, and commands that the indications of this universe be taken, because in this universe there are proofs which point to the planning and decree of Allah. Then the Qur'an, along with the recited revelation and the book of the universe, also makes the important events of human history a source of knowledge and guidance. In human history, the planning and decree of the Divine hand is seen at work. Thus the Qur'an presents humanity before history, and commands that human beings use their senses, their awareness and their faculty of perception to reflect upon history.

Now let us look at the open book of this universe; this surah presents several of its pages. In many places, after presenting the Qur'anic signs of Allah, the book of the universe is presented. Here are some examples:

Al-Mar. Tilka ayat... yu'minun (13:1): "These are the verses of the Book of Allah, and what has been sent down to you from your Lord is the very truth, but most people do not believe."

Allahu alladhi... yuqinun (13:2); wa-huwa alladhi... yatafakkarun (13:3); wa-fi al-ardi... ya'qilun (13:4): "It is Allah who raised the heavens without pillars that you can see, then He established Himself upon the Throne. He subjected the sun and the moon, each running for a term appointed. He directs the affair; He explains the signs in detail, that you may be certain of meeting your Lord. And it is He who spread out the earth, placed upon it firm mountains and rivers, and created of every fruit two mates; He covers the night with the day. In these are signs for people who reflect. And in the earth are adjacent tracts, gardens of grapevines, fields, and palm trees, some single and some in pairs, watered with one water, yet We make some of them superior to others in fruit. In these are signs for people who use reason."

Thus, throughout this surah, scenes are presented from this universe which establish that Allah is its Creator, Owner and Sovereign, and that He is governing this entire universe, and that His system of decree operates within it. After this, the Qur'an admonishes people. They observe all these sights and scenes well, and then they deny that Allah will recreate. They deny revelation on the ground that this Qur'an claims resurrection after death.

Wa-in ta'ajjab fa-'ajab... khalidun (13:5): "If you are to marvel, then marvelous is the saying of those worthy of wonder: 'When we have become dust, shall we indeed be created anew?' These are the ones who have disbelieved in their Lord; these are the ones upon whose necks will be shackles; they are the companions of the Fire, and therein they will abide forever."

Huwa alladhi yurikum... al-thiqal (13:12); wa-yusabbihu al-ra'du... man yasha' (13:13): "It is He who shows you the lightning, causing fear and hope, and who raises up the heavy clouds. The thunder glorifies Him with His praise, and the angels too, in awe of Him. He sends the bolts of lightning and strikes with them whomever He wills."

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 13, verse 43 (part 2 of 3):

Allah presents the pages of this universe before those who dispute about Allah and associate partners with Him, although they observe the signs of Allah's lordship day and night. They constantly witness the signs of Allah's power and His dominion, and they see that this entire universe is obedient to Him. Within this universe He carries out dispositions for the benefit of His servants, and in this universe no one other than Him can carry out any kind of disposition, planning or decree.

﴿وَهُمْ يُجَادِلُونَ فِي اللَّهِ وَهُوَ شَدِيدُ الْمِحَالِ﴾ ﴿لَهُ دَعْوَةُ الْحَقِّ وَالَّذِينَ يَدْعُونَ مِن دُونِهِ لَا يَسْتَجِيبُونَ لَهُم بِشَيْءٍ إِلَّا كَبَاسِطِ كَفَّيْهِ إِلَى الْمَاءِ لِيَبْلُغَ فَاهُ وَمَا هُوَ بِبَالِغِهِ وَمَا دُعَاءُ الْكَافِرِينَ إِلَّا فِي ضَلَالٍ﴾ ﴿وَلِلَّهِ يَسْجُدُ مَن فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ طَوْعًا وَكَرْهًا وَظِلَالُهُم بِالْغُدُوِّ وَالْآصَالِ﴾ ﴿قُلْ مَن رَّبُّ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ قُلِ اللَّهُ قُلْ أَفَاتَّخَذْتُم مِّن دُونِهِ أَوْلِيَاءَ لَا يَمْلِكُونَ لِأَنفُسِهِمْ نَفْعًا وَلَا ضَرًّا قُلْ هَلْ يَسْتَوِي الْأَعْمَىٰ وَالْبَصِيرُ أَمْ هَلْ تَسْتَوِي الظُّلُمَاتُ وَالنُّورُ أَمْ جَعَلُوا لِلَّهِ شُرَكَاءَ خَلَقُوا كَخَلْقِهِ فَتَشَابَهَ الْخَلْقُ عَلَيْهِمْ قُلِ اللَّهُ خَالِقُ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ وَهُوَ الْوَاحِدُ الْقَهَّارُ﴾ (13:13-16) "They dispute about Allah, while He is mighty in strength. To Him is the true call. And those they invoke besides Him do not respond to them with anything, except like one who stretches out his hands toward water to reach his mouth, but it will not reach it. And the supplication of the disbelievers is nothing but in error. And to Allah prostrate whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly and unwillingly, and their shadows at dawn and dusk. Say: Who is Lord of the heavens and the earth? Say: Allah. Say: Then have you taken other than Him as protectors, who possess no benefit or harm for themselves? Say: Are the blind and the seeing alike? Or are darkness and light equal? Or have they attributed to Allah partners who created like His creation, so that the creation seemed similar to them? Say: Allah is the Creator of all things, and He is the One, the Subduer."

Thus this universe becomes a complete exhibition of the proofs of power and the indications of faith. It bestows upon human nature a profound and comprehensive logic and understanding, and this universe addresses the whole human personality. It speaks to all of its faculties of perception, and this dialogue is remarkable, highly logical and well-ordered.

After this, the Noble Qur'an presents human history for human reflection. The Qur'an teaches man that his entire life and its flow are in the hand of Allah's power; Allah is the Ruler, the Subduer, the Disposer, and the One who has complete control.

﴿وَيَسْتَعْجِلُونَكَ بِالسَّيِّئَةِ قَبْلَ الْحَسَنَةِ وَقَدْ خَلَتْ مِن قَبْلِهِمُ الْمَثُلَاتُ وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَذُو مَغْفِرَةٍ لِّلنَّاسِ عَلَىٰ ظُلْمِهِمْ وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَشَدِيدُ الْعِقَابِ﴾ (13:6) "They hasten you toward evil before good, although exemplary punishments have already occurred before them. And indeed, your Lord is full of forgiveness for the people despite their wrongdoing, and indeed your Lord is severe in punishment."

﴿اللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ مَا تَحْمِلُ كُلُّ أُنثَىٰ وَمَا تَغِيضُ الْأَرْحَامُ وَمَا تَزْدَادُ وَكُلُّ شَيْءٍ عِندَهُ بِمِقْدَارٍ﴾ ﴿عَالِمُ الْغَيْبِ وَالشَّهَادَةِ الْكَبِيرُ الْمُتَعَالِ﴾ ﴿سَوَاءٌ مِّنكُم مَّنْ أَسَرَّ الْقَوْلَ وَمَن جَهَرَ بِهِ وَمَنْ هُوَ مُسْتَخْفٍ بِاللَّيْلِ وَسَارِبٌ بِالنَّهَارِ﴾ ﴿لَهُ مُعَقِّبَاتٌ مِّن بَيْنِ يَدَيْهِ وَمِنْ خَلْفِهِ يَحْفَظُونَهُ مِنْ أَمْرِ اللَّهِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يُغَيِّرُ مَا بِقَوْمٍ حَتَّىٰ يُغَيِّرُوا مَا بِأَنفُسِهِمْ وَإِذَا أَرَادَ اللَّهُ بِقَوْمٍ سُوءًا فَلَا مَرَدَّ لَهُ وَمَا لَهُم مِّن دُونِهِ مِن وَالٍ﴾ (13:8-11) "Allah knows what every female carries, and what the wombs diminish and what they increase. Everything with Him is by due measure. He is Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, the Great, the Most High. Whether one of you conceals speech or speaks aloud, and whether one hides by night or goes forth in daylight, it is all the same to Him. For each one are successive [angels] before and behind him who guard him by the command of Allah. Indeed, Allah will not change the condition of a people until they change what is in themselves. And when Allah wills misfortune for a people, there is no repelling it, and they have no protector other than Him."

﴿اللَّهُ يَبْسُطُ الرِّزْقَ لِمَن يَشَاءُ وَيَقْدِرُ وَفَرِحُوا بِالْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا وَمَا الْحَيَاةُ الدُّنْيَا فِي الْآخِرَةِ إِلَّا مَتَاعٌ﴾ (13:26) "Allah extends provision to whom He wills and restricts it. And they rejoice in the worldly life, but the worldly life, compared to the Hereafter, is but a brief enjoyment."

﴿وَلَا يَزَالُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا تُصِيبُهُم بِمَا صَنَعُوا قَارِعَةٌ أَوْ تَحُلُّ قَرِيبًا مِّن دَارِهِمْ حَتَّىٰ يَأْتِيَ وَعْدُ اللَّهِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يُخْلِفُ الْمِيعَادَ﴾ ﴿وَلَقَدِ اسْتُهْزِئَ بِرُسُلٍ مِّن قَبْلِكَ فَأَمْلَيْتُ لِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا ثُمَّ أَخَذْتُهُمْ فَكَيْفَ كَانَ عِقَابِ﴾ (13:31-32) "Those who disbelieve will not cease to be struck by calamity for what they have done, or it will descend near their home, until the promise of Allah comes. Indeed, Allah does not fail in His promise. And messengers before you were certainly ridiculed, but I granted respite to those who disbelieved, then I seized them. So how was My punishment?"

﴿أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْا أَنَّا نَأْتِي الْأَرْضَ نَنقُصُهَا مِنْ أَطْرَافِهَا وَاللَّهُ يَحْكُمُ لَا مُعَقِّبَ لِحُكْمِهِ وَهُوَ سَرِيعُ الْحِسَابِ﴾ ﴿وَقَدْ مَكَرَ الَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِهِمْ فَلِلَّهِ الْمَكْرُ جَمِيعًا يَعْلَمُ مَا تَكْسِبُ كُلُّ نَفْسٍ وَسَيَعْلَمُ الْكُفَّارُ لِمَنْ عُقْبَى الدَّارِ﴾ (13:41-42) "Do they not see that We come to the land, reducing it from its outskirts? And Allah judges, there is no repeller of His judgment, and He is swift in reckoning. And those before them had plotted, but to Allah belongs all planning. He knows what every soul earns, and the disbelievers will know to whom belongs the ultimate home."

Thus, in accordance with its method, the Qur'an presents evidence and insightful arguments from human history, and makes them so effective that collectively they appeal to human nature, and these arguments are presented in a highly organized and ordered manner. From the above explanations we learn a signpost. This is an important sign of the Islamic call, namely that the Qur'an addresses the human personality in an all-encompassing and multi-faceted way. The Qur'an does not address only one aspect of the human personality, such as the aspect of thought and intellect, or the aspect of inspiration and insight, or the aspect of feelings and consciousness. Therefore, we should make the Qur'an the guidebook of the Islamic call. The caller should seek the solution to every problem from the Qur'an before all other sources, and learn from the Qur'an how to call people, in what style and manner, how to give life to dead hearts, and how to ignite souls that have gone cold.

The truth is that the Allah who revealed the Qur'an is the Creator of man. He knows the temperament of man and his makeup. He is aware of the ups and downs of human psychology. He knows where the crookedness lies in those persons. Furthermore, it is the duty of callers to begin their call with the issue of Allah's oneness of divinity and oneness of sovereignty, and to call people that the establishment of Allah's kingship over man is necessary. It is also the duty of these callers to adopt the same method of introducing the Lord, Most High, to people as the Qur'an has adopted, and this method is the truth and reality. They should bring these people to the religion and system of life of Allah, and make them accept that Allah is the One and the only God, that He is also the Lord and the Ruler, and that the system and law that will prevail is the Shariah.

In order to properly acquaint people with Allah and to completely negate every kind of doubt about shirk, the Qur'an adopts this measure: the reality of the Messenger ﷺ is explained before people, and the correct definition of the office of prophethood is presented. The reason is that before Islam, among the People of the Book, the reality of divinity and the reality of prophethood had been mixed together, producing intellectual deviation. The Christians added the attributes of the Divine Being and the attributes of divine sovereignty to the person of Prophet Jesus (peace be upon him). The discussions about the divine and human natures of Jesus (peace be upon him) tore the Christians into pieces. For a long time, several sects grappled with one another.

This confusion did not occur only among Christians; rather, in this field many idolatrous religions were deceived. The concepts of prophethood became incomprehensible. Some people linked prophets with sorcerers. Some equated prophets with mystical philosophers. Some established a relationship between prophets and jinn, and some connected prophets with hidden spirits.

Most of these things existed among the Arab idolaters. Therefore, some people demanded of the Prophet ﷺ that he inform them about the unseen. Some demanded that he show them miracles that break natural habits. Some made specific demands. Some accused him of being a sorcerer, and some said that he had been affected by jinn and was mad. Some demanded that angels accompany him. In short, they issued such challenges and demands and leveled such accusations. All these demands were made because they held an idolatrous, pagan conception of prophethood.

Therefore, the Qur'an spoke at length about the reality of the prophet and the office of prophethood, and explained what the nature of the Messenger is, what the essence of messengership is, and what the reality of divinity is, which belongs to Allah alone without partner, and what the reality of servanthood and worship is, which is found in all kinds and categories of creatures. This servanthood and worship are also embodied in the persons of the prophets (peace be upon them). The prophets (peace be upon them) are also righteous servants of Allah. They are nothing but human beings. None of the attributes that are divine attributes exist in them, and they have no connection or relationship with jinn or any other hidden creature. Only Allah's revelation comes to them, and even with this Islamic revelation they have no authority to display any miracle that breaks natural habits. If any miracle occurs, it occurs by Allah's permission. They are among humans as human beings. The only difference is that Allah has chosen them for the office of messengership, and even after being chosen as prophets and messengers, they remain human beings and servants.

Accordingly, in several places in this surah the station of messengership and the nature of the Prophet are clarified, and it is shown what the limits of the prophet and messenger are. The false conceptions and ideas that idolatrous practices had attached to the person of the Prophet were cleared away, and the stories and mythological tales that were attributed to the prophets were completely negated, which had caused corruption in the beliefs of the People of the Book in particular. Thus this surah completely purified the idolatrous illusions and stories that had entered these institutions.

The Qur'an did not raise these discussions merely as a Godly-and-human philosophy, nor as a philosophical scholarly debate, but these discussions came in response to practical questions arising in the society of that time. Therefore these answers came as a reaction and movement in response to practical challenges, and this was one of the practical struggles within the jihad that was waged at that time, for example:

﴿وَيَقُولُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لَوْلَا أُنزِلَ عَلَيْهِ آيَةٌ مِّن رَّبِّهِ إِنَّمَا أَنتَ مُنذِرٌ وَلِكُلِّ قَوْمٍ هَادٍ﴾ (13:7) "Those who disbelieve say, 'Why has no sign been sent down upon him from his Lord?' You are only a warner, and for every people there is a guide."

﴿وَيَقُولُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لَسْتَ مُرْسَلًا قُلْ كَفَىٰ بِاللَّهِ شَهِيدًا بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَكُمْ وَمَنْ عِندَهُ عِلْمُ الْكِتَابِ﴾ ... "Those who disbelieve say, 'You are not a messenger.' Say, 'Sufficient is Allah as witness between me and you, and whoever has knowledge of the Book.'"

﴿كَذَٰلِكَ أَرْسَلْنَاكَ فِي أُمَّةٍ قَدْ خَلَتْ مِن قَبْلِهَا أُمَمٌ لِّتَتْلُوَ عَلَيْهِمُ الَّذِي أَوْحَيْنَا إِلَيْكَ وَهُمْ يَكْفُرُونَ بِالرَّحْمَٰنِ قُلْ هُوَ رَبِّي لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ عَلَيْهِ تَوَكَّلْتُ وَإِلَيْهِ مَتَابِ﴾ (13:30) "Thus We have sent you to a nation before which nations had passed away, that you might recite to them what We revealed to you while they disbelieve in the Most Merciful. Say, 'He is my Lord; there is no deity except Him. upon Him I rely, and to Him is my return.'"

﴿وَلَقَدْ أَرْسَلْنَا رُسُلًا مِّن قَبْلِكَ وَجَعَلْنَا لَهُمْ أَزْوَاجًا وَذُرِّيَّةً وَمَا كَانَ لِرَسُولٍ أَن يَأْتِيَ بِآيَةٍ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ لِكُلِّ أَجَلٍ كِتَابٌ﴾ (13:38) "And We had already sent messengers before you and gave them wives and descendants, and it was not for a messenger to bring a sign except by the permission of Allah. For every term is a decree."

﴿وَإِن مَّا نُرِيَنَّكَ بَعْضَ الَّذِي نَعِدُهُمْ أَوْ نَتَوَفَّيَنَّكَ فَإِنَّمَا عَلَيْكَ الْبَلَاغُ وَعَلَيْنَا الْحِسَابُ﴾ (13:40) "And whether We show you part of what We promise them or take you in death, your duty is only to convey, and upon Us is the reckoning."

The limits of the office of messengership and the scope of the authority of the Messenger are clarified very well in these verses: that the Messenger is only a warner, his duty is only to convey the message that has come to him to the people and to recite the revelation that comes. He cannot present any miracle without Allah's command. They are servants of Allah; Allah is their Lord as well, and you too must return before Allah. You are human beings like other humans. You married, had children, and lived your humanity and mortality with all its requirements, just as you practically served Allah and fulfilled all the rights of servanthood.

The Qur'an, with complete clarity, cleared from the atmosphere of the world the illusions and superstitions attached to the office of prophethood and the persons of the prophets, and this clouded horizon became clear. The Qur'an negated the self-invented beliefs that the church had attached to the Prophet and prophethood, and to Christ and his mother. Or, as other idolatrous beliefs attached illusions and myths to the prophets, the Qur'an uprooted them completely. Christianity was presented by Prophet Jesus (peace be upon him) in the colour of a true heavenly religion, pure and clean, but within a single century Christianity became a fully idolatrous religion, although Prophet Jesus (peace be upon him) had presented himself only as a servant of Allah.

Before concluding the discussion on this point, it is necessary to reflect on the following verse.

(Commentary of Sayyid Qutb, Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation), on Surah 13, verse 43, part 3 of 3)

And [as for] "Wa in ma nurinnaka ... al-hisab" (13:40): "And O Prophet (ﷺ), whether We show you some part of the evil consequence with which We threaten these people, or We take you (to Ourselves) before its manifestation, in any case your duty is only to convey the message, and the reckoning is Our responsibility."

This statement is addressed to the Prophet upon whom this Qur'an was revealed. You have been commanded to tell people this matter yourself. The summary is that the outcome of the call to religion is not in your own hands, and it is not necessary that religion should prevail and spread through you personally. Your duty is limited to conveying [the message]; giving guidance or not giving it is the work of Allah. Now, whether this work is accomplished during your lifetime or death takes you into its embrace before that, these matters are not among your obligations. Your duty is only that you convey this call to the people. After that, taking the reckoning is the work of Allah. The purpose of this is not that some of the powers of the Prophet (ﷺ) were taken away and his call was restricted, because the obligations of the Messenger (ﷺ) are indeed limited, and the decision rests solely in the authority of Allah.
